# Theory: The Index is a Filter; LFS is a Pointer

Git can store file content as blobs. Ignore rules control which untracked files Git normally offers to add; attributes select behavior for paths, including content filters. LFS stores a pointer blob in Git and keeps the payload separately in local and, after upload, remote LFS storage.

## Invariants

1. `.gitignore` applies to **untracked** files. A tracked file stays tracked until `git rm --cached`.
2. Ignore precedence, from highest to lowest: command-line patterns, applicable in-tree `.gitignore` files, `.git/info/exclude`, and the global excludes file. Within a level, the last matching pattern wins; a deeper `.gitignore` overrides one higher in the tree.
3. `gitattributes` attach behavior to paths: text vs binary, `eol`, `diff`, `merge`, `filter` (clean/smudge).
4. Git LFS stores a **pointer file** (text, few hundred bytes) in Git, and the payload in an LFS object store the forge must provide.

```text
  git add huge.bin     without LFS     blob of huge.bin in .git/objects
  git add huge.bin     with LFS        blob of pointer  version https://git-lfs...
                                       payload ──► LFS store (not in packfiles)
```

## Why Git is a bad backup of videos

A normal full clone generally transfers objects reachable from the refs it fetches, including earlier versions of files; shallow and partial clones can reduce what is transferred. Sparse checkout alone changes which paths appear in the working tree, not necessarily which objects were downloaded. Repeated large binary revisions can substantially increase storage and transfer costs, although compression and delta encoding make the actual size dependent on the content. LFS moves payload transfer to a separate object store; generated artifacts that can be recreated may not need versioning at all.

## What can break

- Ignoring `.env` after it was committed (must `rm --cached`).
- CRLF filters on a Linux-only repo.
- Pushing LFS pointers to a forge with no LFS storage; clones get pointers, not files.

## How to read this chapter

Patterns, attributes, archive, LFS, then a lab. Platform chapters later must store LFS if you use it.
